title: 1. Perf and debug counters behind a build switch
est: ≈4.4k FF + ≈3–4k LUT/ALU (counter adders, readback) · low risk
detail: 32-bit event counters that only the profiler reads: 15 per frame-buffer write buffer (×2), the plane readers' step / burst / stall counters, the memory subsystem's blocked-cycle counters, the texture caches' io_perf, PixelPipeline's debug perf, and RegisterBank's 32 × 32-bit RegNext snapshot copies. Keep the few the board's [perf] line prints; leave the rest to sim (c.trace.enabled) or a GOWIN_PERF switch.

title: 2. PCI ingress stage FIFO is 16 entries of flops
est: ≈700 FF + ≈300 LUT at depth 8 · low risk, check PCI FIFO stalls
detail: PciFifo's ingress.stageFifo (StagedWrite × 16) is built from flops: 1,387 FF + 672 LUT. Halving it, or moving it to one BSRAM (BSRAM is 88% full), is a one-line change; measure 'pci fifo nearly full' on the board before and after.

title: 3. Texture-cache hint queues in flops
est: ≈1.5k FF + ≈700 LUT for both TMUs · medium risk (timing: B193 added an s2mPipe here)
detail: Each TMU's hintIn queue (StreamFifo_10) is 757 FF + 357 LUT. A shallower queue or a BSRAM queue with a registered pop would free most of it; the texture cache tests and the GLQuake trace replay cover the behaviour.

title: 4. DDR3 gate pass maps off (DBG_MAP=0)
est: 512 FF + its readout mux · low risk, debug-only
detail: own_ddr3_ctrl keeps a 128-bit pass map per lane for the debug port (the tool that found the odd-pixel dashes). The gate fix is in; ddrdbg.py dump would lose the maps, but gate positions and status stay. The controller is 5.6k LUT / 3.2k FF overall; its 256-bit a_dq / prev_dq / rd_frame_d1 data path is needed.

title: 5. Texture-coordinate copies in the pixel pipeline
est: ≈1–2k FF · medium effort, needs the sim regression
detail: PixelPipeline's own logic is 5.7k FF, mostly 48-bit S/T/W and gradient fields for both TMUs held in several stages (rasterYPipe fork, rasterYTransformed, the TMU input payloads). Narrowing them to the bits the TMU front end uses, or dropping a copy, is the biggest single-module win left.

title: 6. TMU perspective front end
est: a few hundred FF per TMU · lower confidence
detail: Each TMU's own logic (4k LUT, 2.3k FF, 17 DSP) carries 66-bit S/T products and 48-bit pre/recip values through back-to-back stage registers (…stage_rData and …rData). Synthesis already trims much of the RTL's 6.9k bits; check which copies survive in the netlist first.

title: 7. CLS packing: the real limit
est: unquantified · CLS 85% while LUT 54% and FF 39%
detail: A CLS holds 2 LUTs + 2 FFs that must share clock, enable and reset. With perfect packing this design needs ≈37k CLS; it uses 58.5k. Flops with their own enable / reset (Spinal 'init' on pipeline data, many small stream stages) block packing. Dropping resets from datapath registers in one big block (PixelPipeline) and comparing CLS is a cheap experiment.
